{"basis":"measured","fact_type":"defect","name":"ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): a cause written in a reply reaches no nudge, gate or detector, and the root-cause rule was in no text a consumer project is served, only in reflow2's contributor AGENTS.md","source":"art:kit-instructions","statement":"OBSERVED 2026-10-06, in the dev_reflow2 hub (a consumer project). Asked which unbuilt ideas would be a game changer, the agent wrote that cross-design impact was not built. When Anthony was concerned, it gave two candidate causes and a measurement in chat without the root-cause skill, and he had to ask twice ("Should we do a /root-cause on this?", then "why didn't you run /root-cause? Why did I have to remind you?"). fact:field-feedback-was-triaged-by-reading-a-fourth-time-after-the-rule-and-the-rule-is-delivered-at-no-step counted the 09-18 miss as the fourth reminder, so this is at least the fifth.

MEASURED (step 5), on the session transcript and on origin/main 75ce623df:
(1) Between the answer and the reminder, 7 tool calls (6 Bash, 1 Edit): no skill, no get_skill, no design tool. A cause written only in a reply calls nothing, so every machine trigger reflow2 has was structurally out of reach. record_finding demands the skill (its description and `demanded_by`) but was never called. The loop nudge's PostToolUse hook fired after 47 file edits and is silent until Stop. Its matcher covered one server of seven: about 5 of ~880 design calls. Its four shapes are impact-check (twice), link-artifacts and detect-and-ask; root-cause is none of them. The realized detector (cap:a-fix-with-no-recorded-cause-and-a-defect-its-subject-outran-are-noticed) keys on recorded defect_fix ChangeEvents.
(2) The rule was delivered to no consumer. getting-started/AGENTS.md, the document get_instructions serves (30,285 bytes), mentioned root-cause 0 times, as did the VS Code route file and the handshake. Rule 10 lived only in the repo-root AGENTS.md, which only agents working in reflow2 itself read. The hub's own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md: 0. The 09-07 decision's RULE leg landed for THIS repo only. This is the same shape as fact:root-cause-the-wall-check-was-generalised-in-code-and-never-in-reach-and-the-checkout-cannot-feel-it: the checkout holds the rule, so it cannot feel the absence.
(3) The served skill's trigger text did not reach the agent either. Claude Code truncates each server's handshake about 2,000 characters in, and the catalogue lists root-cause 28th of 32, past the cut. The user-level /root-cause command's description keys on "a failure", while the agent had framed the subject as "not built". The agent's own memory index line said HOW to run it, not WHEN.
(4) get_instructions was called 0 times this session. That would not have helped: the served text had no rule, and since v0.78.0 a plain call returned no document anyway (fact:a-plain-get-instructions-withheld-the-whole-document-from-v0-78-0-and-the-pin-that-would-have-caught-it-was-never-committed-2026-10-06).

CANDIDATES and results:
- C1, the recorded class (an internal-state trigger nothing demands): supported.
- C2, the nudge dark or not naming root-cause: confirmed, see (1).
- C3, the agent runs it only when the user names it: partly refuted. About 30 root-cause investigations were self-started that day, each framed as a failure or a measurement.
- C4, get_instructions never called: true but not causal, see (4).
- C5, token budget: not separable from the transcript.
- C6, it was run and the observation is wrong: refuted, see (1).

CAUSE: the moment "the agent explains in conversation why something does not work" calls no tool, and the one text that names that moment was served to no consumer. Delivery is necessary but not sufficient. The 09-18 miss happened in reflow2's own repo, where rule 10 IS loaded.

REPAIR (chg:the-root-cause-rule-is-served-and-a-plain-get-instructions-returns-the-whole-document): both tiers in the served instructions, near the top; one sentence in the handshake, ending before character 1,200; one paragraph in the VS Code route file; a test pinning all three.
